Fungi are eukaryotic organisms with cell walls that differ from those in plants. Plant cell walls are primarily made of cellulose, while fungal cell walls contain chitin, the same polysaccharide found in the exoskeletons of arthropods.  
Silica is found in the cell walls of diatoms, lignin is a key component in wood (plant cell walls), and collagen fibers are found in animal connective tissues, not fungi.
